welcome.title: Welcome to RentVance
welcome.body: Your properties, the people renting them, and every payment between the two. Here is where everything lives — it takes a minute.

home.title: Your dashboard
home.body: Money in, money out, and anything that needs you this month.

portfolio.title: Your properties
portfolio.body: Every unit you own or manage, one card each.

renters.title: Your renters
renters.body: The people in those units, and the lease behind each one.

money.title: Every payment
money.body: Rent collected and expenses paid, all recorded here.

reports.title: Reports
reports.body: Income against expenses for any period, plus a full expense log.

suppliers.title: Suppliers
suppliers.body: Save the plumber or the management company once, then attach them to any expense.

bell.title: The bell
bell.body: Every alert, with read and unread state.

chat.title: Ask anything
chat.body: Ask about your own portfolio in plain language.

feedback.title: Talk to us
feedback.body: A bug, a question, or an idea — send it from whatever screen you are on, screenshots and all. There is no inbox here; we reply by email to the address on your account.

start.title: Start with one property
start.body: Add it by hand, or scan a lease and we'll create the property and the renter together.

overview.title: What's on this screen
overview.body: Everything Home shows you, one block at a time — starting at the top.

summary.title: The month so far
summary.body: Profit and cash flow, recalculated with every transaction you record.

quickActions.title: Quick actions
quickActions.body: Record rent, log an expense, add a property or a renter — all from here.

attention.title: Needs attention
attention.body: Everything your reminders watch — rent that hasn't arrived, leases about to expire, and any rent changes — shown here the moment they happen. Each row can be acted on without leaving Home.

notifications.title: The same three, on your terms
notifications.body: This button, beside the Needs attention heading, is where those very alerts are set up: which ones go out, when, and to whom. Set once, and they run themselves.

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.body: Which units are let and which are standing empty, at a glance.

recent.title: Recent activity
recent.body: The last few transactions, with the full ledger one click away.

overview.title: Your properties
overview.body: Every unit you manage, however you like to look at them. Here is the screen.

headline.title: The line that counts
headline.body: How many units, how many are occupied, and what they bring in each month.

add.title: Two ways in
add.body: Type a property in yourself, or scan a lease and let us fill it in for you.

select.title: Select more than one
select.body: For the times you need to act on several at once instead of one after another.

persistence.title: Your view stays put
persistence.body: Search, filters and sort are still exactly as you left them the next time you open this screen — nothing resets behind your back.

cards.title: Cards
cards.body: A photo, the rent, and who is in it — built for recognising a place at a glance.

table.title: And the same list as a table
table.body: Watch it change behind this card. Every property on one row — sortable, comparable, better for a long list.

overview.title: Adding a property
overview.body: Address, city and type are all it asks for. Everything else can wait, and can be filled in later from the property itself.

twoSteps.title: Two steps
twoSteps.body: Where it is, then the extras. You can save after the first.

owner.title: Property owner
owner.body: Worth filling in even with one property.

records.title: Bills and paperwork
records.body: Property tax, house committee, meter numbers, the contract itself. None of it is required, and all of it saves you looking things up later.

overview.title: Your renters
overview.body: The people in your properties, and where each lease stands. Here is the screen.

headline.title: The line that counts
headline.body: How many renters you have, and how many leases are running right now.

add.title: Two ways in
add.body: Add a renter and their lease by hand, or scan the lease and let us read it.

ended.title: And who used to
ended.body: Ended tenants have their own filter.

select.title: Select more than one
select.body: For the times you need to act on several renters at once.

search.title: Search stays put
search.body: What you typed and the tab you were on are still here when you come back.

cards.title: Cards
cards.body: A face, a phone number and the lease status — built for recognising a person.

table.title: And the same list as a table
table.body: Watch it change behind this card. Every renter on one row — sortable, comparable, better for a long list.

overview.title: Adding a renter
overview.body: Who they are, then the lease. The lease half is what the rent reminders, the overdue alerts and the reports are all computed from.

extraContacts.title: Anyone else on the lease
extraContacts.body: A guarantor, a partner, a parent paying the rent — add them here with their own phone number, and they are part of the tenancy rather than a note somewhere. Optional, and you can come back to it later.

openEnded.title: Tenancies with no end
openEnded.body: Some tenancies just run — month to month once a contract lapses, or by law in much of Europe. Turn this on and we keep the schedule rolling instead of asking you to invent an end date.

term.title: The term
term.body: Years and months together, so a lease of 1 year and 6 months is entered as easily as one of 2 years. The end date follows from them — it is calculated, never typed.

mode.title: How the rent moves
mode.body: Flat, a fixed percentage, a fixed amount, or your own schedule — whichever of these your country supports.

baseYear.title: Year one
baseYear.body: This is the starting rent. Every later year is computed forward from it.

payment.title: When rent is due
payment.body: The payment day is what 'overdue' is counted from — nothing is charged, it is only the date an alert starts from. Type and frequency just describe how it usually arrives.

overview.title: Every payment, in one place
overview.body: What came in, what went out, and the shape of the last six months. Here is the screen.

hero.title: Six months at a glance
hero.body: Money in against money out, with this month's totals beside it.

filter.title: One kind at a time
filter.body: Narrow the list to money in or money out when you are looking for something specific.

twoKinds.title: Two kinds of money
twoKinds.body: Revenue is rent coming in. Expenses are what you pay out.

forMonth.title: Which month it pays for
forMonth.body: Recorded separately from the date it arrived — March rent can land in April, and the reports still count it as March.

recording.title: Recording rent
recording.body: Every payment that comes in is written down from here.

overview.title: One tenancy, end to end
overview.body: Who the tenant is, what they agreed to pay, what they have actually paid, and the two controls that extend the lease or end it. Here is the screen.

stats.title: This year, and the whole tenancy
stats.body: Revenue and expenses cover the current calendar year, counted by the month each payment is for rather than the day it was entered. Beside them are the lifetime figures and how long this tenant has been here.

tabs.title: Three tabs
tabs.body: The lease itself, the unit they live in, and their money. The tour goes through the first and the last — the middle one is a shortcut to that property.

timeline.title: The lease, year by year
timeline.body: Every period of the lease with the rent for it, in order, including the rises still ahead — so the year that is about to get more expensive is visible now rather than a surprise later. A year whose rent is not yet fixed is marked as a projection.

payments.title: Over on Transactions: did the rent come in?
payments.body: We have moved you to the Transactions tab. Revenue is a month-by-month grid, one box per month, so a month nobody paid for is a hole you can see rather than a number you have to work out.

expenses.title: And what this tenancy cost
expenses.body: Expenses are the other half of the same tab — the toggle above the grid. They are grouped by category rather than by month, because what you spent on a tenant is a different question from whether their rent arrived.

extend.title: Extending, not editing
extend.body: Adds years or months onto the end of the lease and leaves everything already agreed exactly as it is. A tenancy you ended by hand has to be reopened first — extending a terminated lease would quietly un-end it.

end.title: Ending a tenancy
end.body: Marks the lease over from the date you choose, with a reason if there is one. Nothing is deleted: the tenant stays on the property, their payments stay in the reports, and the record can be reopened if it turns out they are staying.

overview.title: Everything about one unit
overview.body: The address and its numbers at the top, and under them a tab each for what you entered, who lives there, the money, and the paperwork. Here is the screen.

stats.title: This year, not all time
stats.body: Net, revenue and expenses cover the current calendar year, counted by the month each transaction is for rather than the day it was entered. The monthly rent beside them is what the lease says today.

tabs.title: Four tabs
tabs.body: What you entered about the place, who lives in it, the money it has made and cost, and the paperwork — one tab each. The tour walks the last three.

renters.title: Who is here, and who was
renters.body: Current tenants first, past ones under them. A tenancy that ends is kept rather than removed, because it is the only record of who paid what while they were here.

payments.title: The money this unit made
payments.body: Rent as a month-by-month grid, one box per month, so an unpaid month is a hole you can see. Expenses sit beside it grouped by category — what a place costs you is a different question from whether the rent came in.

documents.title: Two slots, not a folder
documents.body: A property holds its own basic contract and its land registry extract. The signed lease and the tenant's ID belong to the renter rather than to the unit, so they live on the renter's page.

ask.title: Ask in plain language
ask.body: 'Who hasn't paid this month?' · 'What did I spend on plumbing?'

scope.title: What it can see
scope.body: Your properties, renters and transactions — and nothing outside your account. It reads; it never changes anything.

plan.title: Included on paid plans
plan.body: The assistant comes with every paid plan. On the free plan you can see it here, but asking is switched off until you move up.

base.title: The base index
base.body: We freeze the index at the lease start. Every later change is measured against that number.

lag.title: The index runs late
lag.body: It publishes mid-month for the month before, so a change appears a little after the anniversary. That's the index, not the app.

reanchor.title: Careful with dates
reanchor.body: Changing the lease start later re-anchors the base and re-prices history. If a tenant left early, use End lease instead.

perYear.title: A rule per year
perYear.body: Each year after the first: type an amount, repeat last year, add a percentage, or add a fixed sum.

forward.title: Computed forward
forward.body: Each year builds on the previous year's resolved rent — so an amount you type, then +3%, then a fixed sum, then flat, is expressible exactly.

overview.title: Rent coming in
overview.body: Built for collecting from everyone at once: choose the properties and renters, choose the months, and it writes a row for each.

scope.title: Pick the properties
scope.body: Their renters appear below, each with the rent they owe — taken from that renter's own schedule, so a mid-lease rise is applied for you. Narrow by owner first if you manage for more than one.

period.title: Which months
period.body: One month, a set of months you pick yourself, or a whole contract year. The rows below follow whatever you choose here.

perContract.title: Overriding a row
perContract.body: Every amount is filled in from the contract. Type over any of them for a one-off — a partial payment, a discounted month — and Auto snaps it back.

saving.title: One row at a time
saving.body: A big batch saves as many small writes. If it stops halfway, what was written stays written — re-run only the months that didn't land.

overview.title: Money going out
overview.body: Anything you pay for a property — a repair, a bill, a supplier's invoice. It needs a property, an amount, a date, a payment method and at least one category. Everything else is optional.

split.title: One bill, several units
split.body: Select several properties and the amount splits evenly between them.

required.title: Categories
required.body: At least one, and they are what the reports group by — pick the one you would want a year-end total for. The supplier list narrows to match.

overview.title: Extending a lease
overview.body: Adds years or months onto the end of the lease that is already running. Nothing agreed so far is touched — the existing years stay as they are.

months.title: Years or months
months.body: 'Another three months' is more common than another whole year, so both are here.

optionLast.title: Option years come last
optionLast.body: The preview badges what's new and keeps existing years editable. A contract year after an option year is blocked — a renewal option with binding years after it isn't an option.

overview.title: Suppliers
overview.body: Everyone you pay to keep the properties running, and the expense categories their work files under. Here is the screen.

categories.title: Expense categories
categories.body: They live here too, and they're what your expense reports group by.

what.title: The people you pay twice
what.body: Plumber, electrician, management company. Save once, then attach to any expense.

overview.title: Saving a supplier
overview.body: A name and at least one category is all it needs — the plumber, the electrician, the management company. Save one here and it is offered on every expense from then on, instead of being retyped each time.

categories.title: What they get filed under
categories.body: At least one, and it is what your expense reports group by. When you record an expense the supplier list narrows to whoever matches the category you picked, so getting this right is what makes them easy to find later.

bank.title: Their bank details, for your reference only
bank.body: Nothing here is ever paid, scheduled or sent. RentVance does not move money at all. This is somewhere to keep the account number so it is in front of you when you make the transfer yourself, rather than in a message you have to go looking for.

events.title: Three things we watch
events.body: Rent that hasn't arrived, leases about to expire, and rent changes. Mute any of them, or all of them.

rules.title: Custom rules
rules.body: Change the reminder days and who they apply to.

offsets.title: When
offsets.body: Three days before, seven days after — whatever matches how you actually chase. Type a number and press Enter to add each one; a rule can carry several.

scope.title: Who
scope.body: Everything, or specific owners, properties or renters. A live estimate shows how many renters a rule matches.

cpiException.title: Except CPI
cpiException.body: 'How long before' means nothing for an index that has already moved, so CPI gets a materiality threshold instead of a rule.

placeholders.title: Placeholders
placeholders.body: Tap a chip to drop in the name, amount, address or date. No typing braces.

perLanguage.title: Per language
perLanguage.body: English and Hebrew keep separate versions — editing one never touches the other. Reset restores the original.

overview.title: Reports
overview.body: Two of them, and a record of everything you have exported. Here is the screen.

two.title: Two reports
two.body: Income against expenses for any period, and a full expense log you can filter.

export.title: Export
export.body: Take what you're looking at to your accountant.

pick.title: Start with the document
pick.body: Drop the lease here or click to pick a file — an image, a PDF or a Word document. A lease that runs to several pages can be added a page at a time; they are read as one document. Free accounts get three scans a month, and the count above shows what is left. Then Extract, and we do the reading.

review.title: Nothing saves unread
review.body: We show you every field we found. Fix anything that looks wrong before it is saved.

both.title: Both at once
both.body: One scan can create the property and the renter together — the fastest way in.

seeds.alert-actions: Rows here do more than warn — each one can record the payment or message the renter on WhatsApp without leaving the page.
seeds.scan-lease: Have the lease as a file? Scan it and we'll read it and create the property and the renter in one pass.
seeds.suppliers: Suppliers lives in here too — save the plumber or the management company once, then attach them to any expense.
seeds.reports: Income against expenses for any period, and a full expense log you can filter and export.
seeds.notifications: Rent, expiring leases and rent changes each get their own reminder — change when it fires, or mute it.
seeds.property-owner: Set this if you ever manage units for more than one person — it later filters rent recording and scopes reminders.
seeds.ended-tenants: Past tenants are never deleted. They're under Ended, and search always looks in both.
seeds.bulk-select: Long-press any card to select several at once.
seeds.cpi: CPI links the rent to the Israeli consumer price index. Choose it and we'll explain what that means for your rent.
seeds.custom-schedule: Custom gives every year its own rule — an amount you type, then +3%, then a fixed sum, then flat.
seeds.no-auto-rent: Nothing is charged automatically. 'Overdue' only means no payment is recorded yet — record it and the alert clears itself.
seeds.bulk-rent: Recording rent handles many renters across many months at once. You won't be typing them one by one.
seeds.expense-split: Each property gets its own transaction, so a later correction touches only that one.
seeds.extend-lease: Extend adds years or months and prices them, with a live preview — and it clears the expiring-lease alert for you.
seeds.end-lease: Tenant leaving early? End lease records the exit without rewriting past rent or reports. It's undoable.
seeds.notification-rules: Custom rules change the reminder days and scope them to one owner, property or renter.
seeds.whatsapp-templates: The WhatsApp wording is yours to rewrite, in each language. We never send anything to a tenant — the message lands in your input box, unsent.

callbacks.suppliers: Here's the Suppliers list we mentioned.

hero.headline: Every apartment, every payment, one ledger.
hero.subhead: RentVance tracks rent, expenses and leases for the properties you own, and tells you before a lease renews or a rent changes.
hero.freeNote: Free for up to {{max}} properties. No card needed.

specimen.escalation: Rent rises to ₪5,562 in August, linked to the consumer price index.

lead.heading: Rent that changes on a schedule, worked out for you
lead.body: Most leases do not hold one number for their whole term. RentVance stores the terms — a fixed step each year, or linkage to the consumer price index — and works out what is owed on each date, so you are not rebuilding a lease in a spreadsheet every year. Israeli index linkage is built in.

reports.heading: Reports you can hand to an accountant
reports.body: Income and expenses per property and per period, exported when you need them.

reminders.heading: Told before the date, not after
reminders.body: Lease renewals, rent changes and payments due reach you while you can still act on them.

bilingual.heading: English and Hebrew, both properly
bilingual.body: Full right-to-left support, local date and currency formats, on phone and web.

pricingTeaser.heading: Priced by how many properties you hold
pricingTeaser.body: Free up to {{max}}. Paid plans start where a spreadsheet stops being enough.

pricing.heading: Plans priced by property count
pricing.subhead: Pick the band your portfolio falls into. Move between bands whenever it changes.
pricing.freeBody: Everything in the product, at no cost, for as long as you stay at this size.

included.ledger: Unlimited renters, transactions and expense categories
included.leases: Lease terms with fixed or index-linked rent changes
included.reminders: Reminders for renewals, rent changes and payments
included.bilingual: English and Hebrew, on web, iPhone and Android

pricing.termsBody: Plans are monthly or yearly subscriptions that renew automatically until cancelled. Prices are shown in US dollars; you are charged in your local currency at the rate set by the store or payment provider that sells you the subscription, including any tax that applies where you live. Cancel any time to stop the next renewal — your plan stays active until the period you have paid for ends.

contact.heading: Contact us
contact.subhead: Questions about the product, your account, a payment or a refund — write to us and a person will answer.
contact.responseBody: We aim to reply within two business days. Please include the email address your account uses, so we can find it.
contact.operatorBody: RentVance is operated by Eyal Kook, based in Israel.
